dc_eval_cbrn.note: CBRN weapons capability tested; only 'findings were marginal' from unnamed tests, no score or named test

dc_eval_cyber.quote: we conducted specific tests to determine the capabilities of our models to facilitate the production of weapons (e.g. nuclear, biological, chemical, and cyber)
dc_eval_cyber.note: cyber named as tested; no result beyond 'marginal' from unnamed tests

dc_eval_autonomy.note: no autonomy/AI R&D risk evaluation; tool use is a capability observation

dc_eval_persuasion.note: 'manipulation' appears only as jailbreak attack vectors; misinformation experts on red team but no persuasion/influence-ops evaluation

dc_eval_scheming.note: reward hacking mentioned only as a training problem; no deception/sabotage evaluation

framework_threshold.note: no safety or scaling framework; Responsible Use Guide is deployment guidance

ext_test_any.quote: We conducted a series of red teaming with various groups of internal employees, contract workers, and external vendors.
ext_test_any.note: external vendors and contract workers red teamed the models

ext_test_government.note: no government testing; 'national security agencies' only in related work

ext_test_timing_stated.note: red teaming described as during development/internal releases but not stated as before public release

safeguards_training.quote: We have taken measures to increase the safety of these models, using safety-specific data annotation and tuning
safeguards_training.note: safety SFT, safety RLHF and context distillation

safeguards_runtime.note: only 'code examples ... to apply basic safety techniques at the user input and model output layers', no named mechanism; HateBERT/ToxiGen classifiers used for data analysis and evaluation only

safeguards_access.note: open release under licence/AUP; withholding of the 34B variant for lack of red-teaming time does not apply to the 70B release

safeguards_weights.note: weights openly released; no weight protection
